matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal); you cannot rotate it.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you relocate a stick, ensure its orientation stays the same.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick from a V and placing it as a horizontal stick (invalid orientation change).

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before finalizing a transformation, verify that the total number of sticks remains unchanged.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from an I and not placing it anywhere else.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every symbol must be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a valid operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each proposed move, check that each character still corresponds to a recognized numeral or operator.
matchstick.example: Creating a shape with a single diagonal that does not match any Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and ensure the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a candidate corrected equation, compute its numeric values to confirm it is a true equality.
matchstick.example: Accepting X = XI - X without checking that 10 ≠ 1.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V each consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, each must still contain two diagonals and remain a valid X or V.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a diagonal from X or V, ensure the source character still has two diagonals.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from X, leaving a single diagonal (invalid).

matchstick.title: Within‑numeral stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A stick may be moved to a different position inside the same numeral, altering its shape while keeping it a valid numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you want to change a numeral’s shape without affecting other characters.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal within X to turn it into V.

matchstick.title: Equality sign preservation
matchstick.principle: The '=' sign must remain exactly two horizontal sticks; you cannot alter, add to, or remove from it.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Never move sticks to or from the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Turning '=' into '≠' by removing a horizontal stick.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick transfer
matchstick.principle: A stick may be moved from one character to a different character, altering both; ensure both source and destination remain valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change two characters by moving a stick between them.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from I to '-' to make '+' while leaving I empty.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>', with correct case and whitespace.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the end of your response, output the corrected equation in the required format.
matchstick.example: Providing just the equation without the required prefix.

matchstick.title: Validate single-stick relocation feasibility
matchstick.principle: After proposing a corrected equation, verify that the change from the original can be achieved by moving exactly one stick: the source character loses one stick, the destination character gains one stick, orientations are preserved, and all characters remain valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After generating a candidate equation, compare it to the original to ensure only one stick has been moved and all constraints are satisfied.
matchstick.example: Proposing 'XVII = XVIII - I' which is mathematically correct but would require moving multiple sticks; this violates the single‑stick move rule.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model often checks only the visual plausibility of the transformed equation and forgets to compute the numeric values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always convert both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and confirm the equality before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model outputs the corrected equation without the required prefix or does not place it as the last line.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure the final line of the response is exactly 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>' with proper case and spacing.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a character but does not place it elsewhere, effectively deleting a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When moving a stick, always specify a destination character where the stick will be added.

matchstick.description: Breaking a numeral by moving a stick away (including I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick from a numeral that consists of a single stick (I) or from X/V, leaving the source character invalid.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only move a stick from a numeral that will remain a valid Roman numeral after losing that stick; never take the only stick from I.

matchstick.description: Proposed equation not reachable by a single stick move (multiple sticks changed)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model proposes a mathematically correct equation but changes several characters, which would require moving more than one stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After proposing a corrected equation, compare it to the original and ensure that exactly one stick has been moved; no other characters should be altered.
